title: Classic Creamed Spinach
summary: Baby spinach wilted with shallot and garlic, simmered in cream and thickened with a butter-flour paste, finished with nutmeg.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Mash the softened butter and flour together with a fork until completely smooth. This paste thickens the cream without lumps, because the butter keeps the flour particles apart as they disperse.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Melt the remaining 30 g butter in the pot over medium heat and soften the shallot and garlic for 1-2 min until translucent. Add the spinach a handful at a time with the salt, turning with tongs, and cook about 4 min until just wilted.

steps.title: Thicken the cream
steps.text: Pour in the cream and bring it to a simmer. Stir in the butter-flour paste and cook for about 3 min, until the sauce thickens and coats the leaves rather than running off them.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the pepper and nutmeg, then taste for salt. Spoon into a warm shallow dish and serve while hot.

tips: Baby spinach needs no chopping; with mature spinach, remove the tough stems and chop the leaves.
Add the spinach in handfuls so it wilts evenly instead of steaming in a heap.
Do not boil the sauce hard after adding the paste, or it can turn gluey.
A little grated hard cheese adds richness if you want it.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan, stirring and adding a splash of milk if thick, until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
